newsitem.title: UK: UK's Cook to press Bosnia leaders on peace process.
newsitem.headline: UK's Cook to press Bosnia leaders on peace process.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook visits Bosnia next week to deliver a blunt warning to the Balkan state's multi-ethnic leadership about lack of progress in implementing the 1995 Dayton peace accords.

"I expect some frank exchanges -- particularly on the need for reintegration within the Dayton framework, but also on war criminals, corruption and media freedom," the foreign secretary said in a statement.

Cook also wants to show support for Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic in her power struggle with ultra-nationalists loyal to former president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic, British officials said.

One official said Cook was prepared for hardline Bosnian Serbs to "make a noise" during his visit next Tuesday because of the swoop on two war crimes suspects on July 10 by British troops in the 30,000-strong NATO-led peacekeeping force.
A Bosnian Serb police chief was killed in the raid, which Cook said showed Britain's determination to bring war criminals to justice in accordance with the Dayton peace agreement.
"The British have shown in recent days that they're prepared to act as well as to talk," a senior British official said.
He said Cook would bluntly tell Bosnia's leaders that progress to date in normalising civilian life in the war-torn country had been "seriously inadequate".

Under the Dayton accords, Bosnia is supposed to be a single state comprising two separate entities, one for Serbs and the other a Moslem-Croat federation. But ethnic factions are resisting integration.

Cook will meet the three members of Bosnia's rotating presidency -- Alija Izetbegovic, a Muslim, Kresimir Zubak, a Croat, and Momcilo Krajisnik, a Serb -- in Sarajevo and urge action on issues including military liaison, the appointment of ambassadors and the issuance of passports.
Britain backs Plavsic because she is relatively keen on the Dayton process, but it does not harbour any illusions.
"Plavsic is no angel," the senior official said. "But you have to make bread with the small amount of flour you've got, and that's where we are."
Cook will hold talks with Plavsic in her fief of Banja Luka, where he will spend the night with British troops before travelling to Croatia on Wednesday for talks with President Franjo Tudjman.
